pull_request.title: Tracker: Define default module placements with coverage and transverse views
pull_request.head: study/cobe-pint-module-coverage
pull_request.body:
The reviewer requested a concrete working default and transverse views after the finite-module cobe/pint comparison. This PR now supplies that default, two independently configurable barrel options, reproducible coverage checks and actual x-y sections. It remains an isolated DES-009 PROTOTYPE.

The default uses cobe's cylindrical layers: tangential phi-staggered pixels with no z staggering; tangential phi/z-staggered short strips; common-radius long-strip staves with 12° local phi tilt and no z staggering; and clearance-staggered endcaps. The user explicitly confirmed that “no tilt section” means omitting inclined barrel sections by default, and that the unnamed third barrel bullet means long strips. Engineering assumptions are explicit in the report; no detector sign-off is inferred.

- [Reviewer-directed default, results and figures](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/study/cobe-pint-module-coverage/docs/validation/DES-009-review-default.md)
- [Barrel x-y sections](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/study/cobe-pint-module-coverage/docs/validation/DES-009-review-default/views/barrel-sections.png) and [module details](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/study/cobe-pint-module-coverage/docs/validation/DES-009-review-default/views/barrel-detail.png)
- [Representative endcap tiling](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/study/cobe-pint-module-coverage/docs/validation/DES-009-review-default/views/endcap-reference.png), with normal staggering levels and physical/active boundaries distinguished
- [Repeatable workflow](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/study/cobe-pint-module-coverage/tools/module_layout/README.md) and [classified design inputs](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/study/cobe-pint-module-coverage/docs/design/DES-009-module-populated-layouts.md)

The new 2×2 comparison switches pixel z staggering and short-strip phi tilt independently. Nine scan cases total 169,344 trajectory evaluations: the full luminous-box/angular grid, an independent random check, and a default-only total-p check. All four placements have zero trial-body clashes and host overruns. All nine native ACTS audits pass: 432 tracks and 382,142 candidate targets with exact reached-patch agreement. The default uses 24,855 modules and 217.465 m² gross sensor surface, with 5.9–6.3% missing eligible stations on the independent sample. Its combined long-barrel policy saves silicon but loses coverage; the report shows that cost explicitly. The tested short-strip tilt performs worse than tangential staggering, so tangential remains default. Pixel z staggering is retained as an option.

A rejected 26-row placement caused 328 long-barrel/endcap body clashes. The documented end-fit amendment uses full modules at a uniform compatible pitch, preserves the ideal-layer endpoints and retains honest longitudinal gaps. The rejected control is preserved. True section plots retain empty seams rather than projecting unrelated z rows into the section.

The [original 32-case cobe/pint comparison](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/study/cobe-pint-module-coverage/docs/validation/DES-009-module-populated-layouts.md), with 477,312 trajectory evaluations and 1,534 native audit tracks, remains unchanged as historical evidence. Inputs come from pinned pixel/strip proposals #8/#21/#22. Native propagation uses the isolated binding overlay from draft [acts-project/acts#6178](https://github.com/acts-project/acts/pull/6178); full global navigation, material/reconstruction performance and engineered supports remain unvalidated.

Validation: 41 local geometry/intersection/sampling/native/section tests; exact same-platform comparison of all 12 legacy geometry outputs with the frozen previous generator; 27 dashboard tests, 32 logging tests, 14 browser assertions, report/view export checks, dashboard build and session validation. Public CI runs numerical controls and explicitly skips native ACTS tests when unavailable. Updated tracking, review records, provenance and paired logs preserve the exact review target and approval boundary.

comments.body:
After reviewing, I think we should go on with the following next steps:

Defaults:
- no tilt section as default (to simplify stave results)

* Barrel*:
- phi staggered pixel barrel ( z -staggering to be checked as a second option)
- phi staggered short strip barrel ( either with tilt or tangential modules with different radii), z-staggering as default
- phi staggered with tilt, no z-staggering in the barrel to make stave building easy 

*Endcap*
- staggering throughout, to be checked later if feasible.

Please make a default design like this, which we will move forward.

This time, please make x-y cross sections of the barrel, and also make x-y tiled views of the endcap (one reference endcap is enough)

Implemented the requested working default and added the transverse views.

- **Pixels:** tangential phi staggering, no z staggering by default; z staggering remains a separate option.
- **Short strips:** tangential modules at alternating radii with z staggering by default; common-radius local phi tilt is retained as an alternative.
- **Long strips:** common-radius staves with 12° local phi tilt and no z staggering.
- **Endcaps:** staggering throughout, retaining the cleared trial boxes; support/services feasibility remains open.

The user explicitly confirmed that “no tilt section” means no inclined section by default, and that the third unnamed barrel bullet means long strips. The default therefore uses the unchanged cobe cylindrical layers. This clarification is recorded; formal detector sign-off remains separate.

The [new report](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/study/cobe-pint-module-coverage/docs/validation/DES-009-review-default.md) contains [barrel x-y sections](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/study/cobe-pint-module-coverage/docs/validation/DES-009-review-default/views/barrel-sections.png), [module details](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/study/cobe-pint-module-coverage/docs/validation/DES-009-review-default/views/barrel-detail.png), and [reference endcap tiling](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/study/cobe-pint-module-coverage/docs/validation/DES-009-review-default/views/endcap-reference.png). These are actual barrel cuts at labelled z positions; the endcap figure explicitly projects all staggering levels. The outer-pixel inter-module gap at z=0 remains visible, with all four pixel layers appearing in the second cut.

The default has **24,855 modules and 217.465 m² of gross sensor surface**. All four default/option combinations have zero trial-box and host conflicts. The new scans cover **169,344 trajectories**, and all **nine ACTS audits pass** on 432 sampled tracks. Independent-sample station losses are **5.970 / 5.897 / 6.302%** for straight / positive / negative tracks. The simpler combined long-barrel policy has a clear coverage cost; it is quantified in the report. Pixel z staggering gives a modest gain, while the tested short-strip tilt increases losses and depth, supporting the tangential default.

A full-row minimum-pitch trial collided with the first long-strip endcap; the retained rejected control and documented endpoint-fit rule explain the correction. Original cobe/pint evidence is preserved. Shape inputs, the 2×2 scan and figure generation are repeatable through the [workflow](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/study/cobe-pint-module-coverage/tools/module_layout/README.md). Local native/unit/integration checks passed, and [PR CI passed](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/actions/runs/36545667460) at evidence revision `01b8e229663f117fb22d98f90af4b932312b6979`.

User requests, paraphrased: populate cobe/pint using working pixel and strip
module models; compare staggering, tilts and flat staves; evaluate hits,
hermeticity and silicon for straight and 1 GeV tracks in 3 T over the specified
luminous region; divide work among subagents and recommend where support
complexity is beneficial. The user authorized creating a PR and Git/GitHub use.
Exact additional request: “Also, make this workflow repeatable, in case we have
future updates to the module/sensor shapes”. Earlier conditional authorization
requested an ACTS draft PR if needed functionality was missing.

The assistant asked an optional pT-versus-total-p clarification. No answer was
received; pT = 1 GeV was stated as the primary convention, then a separate
total-p = 1 GeV check was added so both interpretations are measured.

events.text:
The working models are explicit rectangular active masks, pixel chip islands,
and long-strip same-module stereo pairs. Pixel outlines/guards/services remain
conditional fixtures. New JSON dimensions and sampling controls drive a fresh
run directory; unsupported shapes fail explicitly. No production geometry,
reconstruction setting or human approval changed.

Four initial patterns exposed body clashes. Two mechanically motivated
clearance variants add pixel-endcap depth colours and account for barrel
curvature; all four cleared cobe/pint combinations pass trial-box and host checks.
The failed controls remain. Short-strip barrel staggering gives a clear coverage
gain. Long-strip staggering has substantial silicon/depth cost; pixel barrel
losses remain significant. Pint's full inclined modules overhang their ideal
segments, which is retained and reported.

The pooled grids showed phase-dependent charge asymmetries. An independent
4,096-direction sample confirms the support ranking without interpreting the
probe distribution as collider event efficiency. A separate 12,288-trajectory
rerun reproduced all numerical metrics exactly.

Native ACTS exposed two distinct issues. A single giant TryAll navigation leaf
misses curved-track candidate surfaces; the adverse control is retained and is
not described as validated global navigation. Target propagation also needed a
maximum step control unavailable in the Python options. A temporary native
guide-state method passed all 32 preliminary case audits. A separate isolated
ACTS worktree adds the small step-size binding and genuine propagation tests;
its compiled overlay leaves the shared installation/source/build untouched.
Final study runs use the preferred direct target propagation with that option.
Both methods distinguish finite-surface intersection checks from global navigation.
